title: Dietary Arthrospira platensis as a Sustainable Fishmeal Alternative Enhances Growth Performance, Body Composition and Muscle Amino Acid and Fatty Acid Profiles of Pearl Spot (Etroplus suratensis)
content:
ABSTRACT

The increasing cost and limited availability of fishmeal have intensified the search for sustainable alternative protein sources for aquafeeds. Arthrospira platensis, owing to its high-quality protein and bioactive compounds, has emerged as a promising substitute for fishmeal. This study evaluated the effects of graded dietary A. platensis inclusion on growth performance, feed utilization, body composition and muscle amino acid and fatty acid profiles of juvenile Etroplus suratensis. A 60-day feeding trial was conducted using juveniles (13.39 ± 0.13 g) reared in aerated fiberglass-reinforced plastic tanks under 6 ppt salinity and fed five isonitrogenous and isoenergetic diets in which Spirulina replaced fishmeal protein at 0% (SP0), 25% (SP25), 50% (SP50), 75% (SP75) and 100% (SP100). The treatments were done in triplicate tanks. Growth performance and feed utilization were significantly influenced by dietary treatments (p < 0.05), with SP50 producing the highest final weight gain (13.48 ± 0.16 g), specific growth rate (0.98%), protein efficiency ratio (0.35), feed conversion efficiency (0.67) and the lowest feed conversion ratio (1.48). Survival remained relatively high across all treatments. Spirulina supplementation significantly enhanced carcass crude protein while reducing whole-body lipid and moisture contents (p < 0.05). Muscle essential amino acids, particularly leucine, methionine, lysine, valine and histidine, were optimized at moderate inclusion levels, especially SP50. Dietary Spirulina significantly improved lipid quality by increasing polyunsaturated fatty acids, including eicosapentaenoic acid, docosahexaenoic acid, total n − 3 and n − 6 fatty acids, with maximum values generally observed at SP75. In conclusion, replacing fishmeal with Spirulina at 50%–75% significantly improved growth performance, feed efficiency and the nutritional quality of pearl spot without compromising survival. These findings demonstrate that Spirulina is a sustainable functional ingredient for aquafeeds, with 50% replacement recommended for optimal growth and 75% for enhanced muscle nutritional quality and health-promoting fatty acid composition.
